For too long, certain individuals have presented themselves as political heavyweights, relying on big names, exaggerated claims of influence, and perceived proximity to power, without establishing a sustainable political foundation among Zamfara’s electorate.
However, the realities of politics are gradually revealing the difference between genuine political strength and artificial political relevance. Politics is not sustained by publicity alone. It is built through consistent engagement with the electorate, investment in party structures, respect for political stakeholders, and the ability to maintain meaningful relationships with people at the grassroots.
Those who mistook media visibility for political acceptance may eventually realise that public recognition does not automatically translate into electoral strength. The emerging political realities in Zamfara North, marked by the emergence of Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, suggest that the era of political grandstanding without a solid foundation may be drawing to a close.
One of the greatest lessons of democratic politics is that political influence must be earned, nurtured, and sustained. A politician who cannot command genuine loyalty within their immediate political environment may find it difficult to exercise influence beyond it. Similarly, individuals who base their political relevance on personal ambition rather than collective interests often struggle when tested by the realities of party politics and electoral competition.
The changing political climate in Zamfara also presents an opportunity for genuine political leaders, such as His Excellency Senator Abdul’aziz Yari Abubakar, to consolidate their structures, strengthen party unity, and reconnect with the people. Political leadership should be determined not by who makes the loudest claims or dominates social media discussions, but by who has consistently demonstrated commitment, capacity, experience, and the ability to deliver results.
The political experience and organisational networks of Senator Abdul’aziz Yari Abubakar (Marafan Sokoto), for instance, demonstrate the importance of long-term political engagement, party organisation, and sustained relationships with political stakeholders.
Ultimately, the onset of a political eclipse does not necessarily mean the immediate disappearance of certain political figures; rather, it signals the gradual loss of relevance among those whose political identities are greater than their actual grassroots influence.
In politics, a big name without a solid political foundation is merely a temporary illusion of power. When the people withdraw their confidence, political titles lose their significance, publicity loses its value, and the so-called political giants begin to experience the reality of political eclipse. Some seemingly political heavyweights only sustain relevance for as long as they remain in the political offices to which they are appointed.
